argument: The Protection trio at 643, 650 and 657 reuses three card names the divine chapter already owns at 12:161, 12:197 and 12:220, with the same Discipline counts, the same DR steps and the same upkeep sentence, so the book now ships two identically titled ladders. The family's own precedent says a later tradition gets fresh names: when the primal branch of that same ladder was written it was renamed at 12:170, 12:204 and 12:227, and nothing about the arcane trio needs the divine wording to function. The bill comes due in the armor chapter, which cites the ladder bare at 16:33, 16:102 and 16:108; a reader following those examples cannot say which chapter's card they need, and every other surface is mute: a heading sweep of all chapters returns exactly three cross-chapter card-name collisions, all three this trio (11:643 with 12:161, 11:650 with 12:197, 11:657 with 12:220), while a grep of the glossary and the reference sheets for the three names returns zero hits, so nothing downstream settles the question. Minimal fix: rename the arcane three on the primal pattern, or delete them, since a divine or primal caster already buys identical numbers at an identical price.

evidence.claim: The divine file prints the same three card names at 12:161, 12:197 and 12:220, keyed to Protection and carrying the same values as the arcane trio at 643, 650 and 657.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Bark Skin, Stone Skin, and Iron Skin

evidence.claim: When the primal version of this ladder was added it received three fresh names rather than the divine titling, at 12:170, 12:204 and 12:227.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Beast Hide, Scaled Hide, and Carapace

evidence.claim: The armor chapter's worked examples cite the ladder with no tradition marker at 16:33, 16:102 and 16:108, so a reader cannot tell which of the two identically named cards is meant.
